title: Xi Jinping's Thought on Ecological Civilization: Its Original Contribution to Marxist Ecological Theory and Its Practical Expansion
journal: Lecture Notes in Education Psychology and Public Media
abstract: Xi Jinping's Thought on Ecological Civilization represents the latest achievement of the Sinicization and modernization of Marxist ecological theory. It systematically addresses the major issues of why ecological civilization should be built in the new era, what kind of ecological civilization should be built, and how it should be built. This paper takes Marxist basic principles as its foundation and, around the dimensions of natural wealth, people's position, ecological justice, carbon governance, digital governance, Party leadership, and global ecological governance, elucidates its original contributions to the theory of productive forces, the laws of socialist construction, the national governance system, and the global ecological discourse. The study finds that Xi Jinping's Thought on Ecological Civilization takes the harmonious coexistence of man and nature as its value orientation, green new-quality productive forces as its practical support, and institutional advantages and international dissemination as important guarantees, providing scientific guidance for promoting the construction of Beautiful China and building a clean and beautiful world.

title: Writing down my nickname: the role of name reminders in shaping consumer behavioral intentions
journal: Asia Pacific Journal of Marketing and Logistics
abstract: Purpose This study aims to theoretically and empirically investigate how name reminders influence consumer behavioral intentions and explore the underlying mechanism and boundary condition of this effect. Design/methodology/approach Four scenario-based experiments (two offline and two online) were conducted to examine the effects of different forms of name reminders on consumer behavioral intentions. The mediating role of self-brand connection and the moderating role of typeface were tested. Findings The results indicate that name reminders, particularly nicknames, significantly enhance consumer behavioral intentions. Specifically, the use of name reminders and nicknames produces stronger positive effects than no name reminders and formal name reminders. The findings further demonstrate that self-brand connection mediates this effect and that the effectiveness of name reminders is moderated by typeface. Originality/value This study theoretically and empirically explains how intimate relationship cues conveyed through name reminders influence consumer behavioral intentions. It enriches the literature by conceptualizing different types of name reminders (nicknames vs formal names) as distinct relational cues and by clarifying the underlying psychological mechanism. The findings also offer actionable implications for firms and policymakers seeking to strengthen long-term consumer relationships through strategically designed personalized communication.

title: Weighting risk impact indicators in a food system: expert elicitation and analysis prior to inclusion in a multi-risk assessment
abstract: Abstract To cover the farm-to-fork continuum of a food system, it is necessary to tackle a range of risks associated with different domains, such as agriculture, environment, economics, nutrition and food safety. In each domain, several risk impact indicators are required, for instance in the food safety domain, several hazards (leading to a risk) have to be considered: pathogenic bacteria, heavy metals, etc. Obtaining the data to score the indicator is a scientific work that requires data and models. However, that is not enough: to aggregate the risk impact indicators, weights must be assigned to each indicator. In this study, the lentil food system was chosen as case-study, considering that its production and consumption may increase in the future. The expert elicitation process was conducted within a boarder Living Lab experience to address the inherent subjectivity of weighting procedures, while ensuring transparency, inclusiveness, and reflexivity in expert-based decision support. A group of 11 experts were interviewed regarding weights associated with 16 risk impact indicators. Their responses were scored along with their level of knowledge on each indicator, and then a more in-depth analysis was carried out to establish the weights for each indicator. The weights are presented as a probability distribution representing the variability in the 10 expert judgements, adjusted for the uncertainty (more exactly the lack of certainty) in their belief. This method for obtaining and analysing risk impact indicator weights, brings objectivity, transparency and robustness and then brings an added-value to a multi-risk assessment.

The Impact of Green Finance Reform and Innovation Pilot Zone Policy on Corporate ESG Performance: A Case Study of Huayou Cobalt
journal: Advances in Economics, Management and Political Sciences
abstract: Whether and how the green finance innovation reform pilot zones policies (GFRPZP)affect the ESG performance of micro enterprises is an important topic in green finance research. This paper takes Huayou Cobalt, a company registered in the first batch of pilot zones, as a case, and adopts a longitudinal single-case study method to construct an analytical framework of three transmission paths: "financing constraints - information disclosure - green innovation", to investigate the mechanism by which the policies affect the ESG performance of enterprises. The research findings show that GFRPZP, through differentiated green loans and green bond issuance, effectively reduced the green financing costs of enterprises, and shifted the financing structure from mainly short-term to a balance of both short and long terms; the mandatory environmental information disclosure requirement prompted enterprises to upgrade their reporting systems from qualitative descriptions to international quantitative disclosure, forcing the improvement of ESG management capabilities; the facilitation of green finance reduced the funding threshold for green technology research and development, and enabled enterprises to make breakthroughs in clean energy, water resource recycling, and carbon emission reduction of products. These three paths form a mutually reinforcing mechanism - increased R&D investment improves environmental performance, information disclosure reduces financing costs, and abundant funds then feedback to technological innovation, ultimately driving the continuous improvement of the enterprise's ESG comprehensive performance.

title: Rethinking the quadruple helix in place-based innovation: power, space and public experience
journal: Journal of Place Management and Development
abstract: Purpose The paper aims to explore how stakeholder governance dynamics shape public experiences in innovation district spaces. It addresses a gap in the public lifeworld by interrogating the quadruple helix model of innovation and its spatial consequences. Design/methodology/approach Qualitative interviews with community council representatives and residents in two Glasgow innovation districts were analysed thematically through the lens of social space theory. Findings From the public’s perspective, innovation districts are governed unequally. This reinforces the production of districts as territorial enclaves and as spaces of urban colonisation, privileging institutional interests and capitalist logics while marginalising existing communities. Originality/value The study provides a public-centred critique of the quadruple helix model of innovation, linking power dynamics to lived spatial experiences. It conceptualises innovation districts as territorial enclaves and as colonial landscapes. Ultimately, it calls for more meaningful public inclusion to confront enduring urban divisions.

title: Understanding the developer and user perspectives of design pattern detection tools
abstract: Abstract Design Pattern Detection (DPD) tools are useful to support to the comprehension and maintenance of software systems. Although several DPD tools have been introduced over the years, they typically focus on a limited set of design patterns and programming languages. This paper aims to investigate (i) the reasons that motivate DPD tool designers to target specific design patterns and programming languages, and (ii) how potential users perceive the usefulness of DPD tools in practical software development scenarios. We conducted two online surveys. For the first survey, we reached out to designers of 42 DPD tools selected from a systematic literature review to obtain their perspectives on design decisions about pattern and language coverage, receiving 22% of such responses. For the second survey, we recruited 28 student and senior developers to help us understand their expectations, perceived benefits, and concerns related to the use of DPD tools. Within our sample, the findings suggest that participating tool designers often prioritize design patterns whose internal structure facilitates automated detection, while language support is frequently motivated by popularity and expected demand. From the perspective of tool users, DPD tools are expected to support development activities, such as program comprehension and software quality improvement. Unfortunately, usability difficulties, limited accuracy, and insufficient documentation often discourage them from adopting a tool. The responses suggest that some design decisions reported by participating DPD tool designers are aligned with practical and industrial considerations. However, the recurring lack of adequate documentation and usability support is a major barrier to wider usage. Taken as indicative evidence, these results suggest that future DPD tools should better balance detection capabilities and usability concerns, especially to meet the need of less experienced developers. Given the limited number of tool-designer respondents, conclusions about design rationale should be interpreted as indicative rather than representative of all DPD tool designers.
